entry.title: Show HN: Levee - a self-tuning circuit breaker and concurrency limiter for Go (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Rate limiters and circuit breakers work wonderfully well when they're configured for the load and available capacity. But load, capacity, and latency drift over time, and keeping those settings current requires continuous effort. So I built Levee to be a hands-off, adaptive, easy to configure traffic governor. Levee is configured with a success-rate target and timeout. It then continuously monitors the workload performance characteristics to detect downstream capacity exhaustion or failures. It can also spot a surge from growing concurrency before failures arrive. It runs in-process, uses a small, fixed amount of memory, has zero dependencies, and processes millions of requests per second. In a deterministic 10-node mesh simulation, Levee outscored carefully tuned static rate limiters/breakers deployed throughout the mesh, while recording fewer failures and no node crashes. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48877437 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: Ant - A JavaScript runtime and ecosystem (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Hello HN! I'm the author of Ant, a JavaScript ecosystem built around a runtime with its own JavaScript engine. Ant also includes a package manager, the ants.land package registry, a platform for deploying and hosting applications, and Ant Desktop for building native desktop apps with web technologies, similar to Electron. The goal is for these pieces to work as one coherent platform while remaining compatible with the wider JavaScript ecosystem. It's still early, and I'd appreciate any feedback on the overall direction or what you'd like to see from an e2e alternative to the existing JavaScript stacks. P.S. I've shared Ant here before as a runtime; since then, it has grown into the broader ecosystem you see today. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48875377 Points: 176 # Comments: 77

The app includes more than 15,000 objects tracked by CelesTrack, together with their pass predictions, descriptions, and detailed orbital data.
